citations.quote: h:=\psi^4\bar h,\qquad K:=\frac{\tau}{3}h+\psi^{-2}\bar A,\qquad E:=\psi^{-6}\bar E,\qquad B:=\psi^{-6}\bar B
Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature.

derivations.claim: In any positively oriented coordinate chart, $\det h=\psi^{12}\det\bar h$, so $\sqrt{\det h}=\psi^6\sqrt{\det\bar h}$. The Levi-Civita formula and the determinant derivative give $\Gamma^i{}_{ik}=\partial_k\log\sqrt{\det h}$, hence $D_iV^i=(\sqrt{\det h})^{-1}\partial_i(\sqrt{\det h}\,V^i)$ for every smooth vector field $V$. Substituting $V=E=\psi^{-6}\bar E$ and then $V=B=\psi^{-6}\bar B$ gives $D_iE^i=\psi^{-6}\bar D_i\bar E^i$ and $D_iB^i=\psi^{-6}\bar D_i\bar B^i$. Since $e=\alpha^{-1}E$, $b=\alpha^{-1}B$, and both factors are positive, the two SI divergence constraints are equivalent to the two barred divergence equations.

The oriented volume forms satisfy $\operatorname{vol}_h=\psi^6\operatorname{vol}_{\bar h}$. In coordinates, $(E\times_hB)_i=(\operatorname{vol}_h)_{ijk}E^jB^k=\psi^{-6}(\bar E\times_{\bar h}\bar B)_i$. Also $|E|_h^2=\psi^{-8}|\bar E|_{\bar h}^2$ and $|B|_h^2=\psi^{-8}|\bar B|_{\bar h}^2$, by inserting $h_{ij}=\psi^4\bar h_{ij}$ and the two vector weights. Therefore $(\kappa/\mu_0)(|e|_h^2+|b|_h^2)=2\psi^{-8}(|\bar E|_{\bar h}^2+|\bar B|_{\bar h}^2)$ and $(\kappa/\mu_0)(e\times_hb)_i=2\psi^{-6}(\bar E\times_{\bar h}\bar B)_i$, using [F3].

Taking the $h$-trace of $K=(\tau/3)h+\psi^{-2}\bar A$ gives $\operatorname{tr}_hK=\tau+\psi^{-6}\bar h^{ij}\bar A_{ij}=\tau$, because $\bar A$ is trace-free. In the squared norm, the cross term between $(\tau/3)h$ and $\psi^{-2}\bar A$ vanishes by the same trace condition; the pure trace term is $\tau^2/3$, and the trace-free term is $\psi^{-12}|\bar A|_{\bar h}^2$. Thus $|K|_h^2=\tau^2/3+\psi^{-12}|\bar A|_{\bar h}^2$.

Put $u=2\log\psi$, so $h=e^{2u}\bar h$. In a chart, metric compatibility and torsion-freeness give $\Gamma[h]^k{}_{ij}=\tfrac12h^{k\ell}(\partial_i h_{j\ell}+\partial_j h_{i\ell}-\partial_\ell h_{ij})$, hence $C^k{}_{ij}:=\Gamma[h]^k{}_{ij}-\Gamma[\bar h]^k{}_{ij}=\delta^k_i u_j+\delta^k_j u_i-\bar h_{ij}u^k$. Expanding the curvature definition and contracting gives $\operatorname{Ric}(h)_{ij}=\operatorname{Ric}(\bar h)_{ij}+\bar D_kC^k{}_{ij}-\bar D_iC^k{}_{kj}+C^k{}_{ij}C^\ell{}_{k\ell}-C^k{}_{i\ell}C^\ell{}_{kj}$. Here $C^k{}_{kj}=3u_j$, $\bar D_kC^k{}_{ij}=2\bar D_i u_j-\bar h_{ij}\bar\Delta u$, and $\bar D_iC^k{}_{kj}=3\bar D_i u_j$ because $du$ is closed. Expanding the products gives $C^k{}_{ij}C^\ell{}_{k\ell}=6u_i u_j-3\bar h_{ij}|du|_{\bar h}^2$ and $C^k{}_{i\ell}C^\ell{}_{kj}=5u_i u_j-2\bar h_{ij}|du|_{\bar h}^2$; tracing with $h^{ij}=\psi^{-4}\bar h^{ij}$ therefore yields $R(h)=\psi^{-4}(\bar R-4\bar\Delta u-2|du|_{\bar h}^2)$. Substitution of $u=2\log\psi$ and $\bar\Delta\log\psi=\psi^{-1}\Delta_{\bar h}\psi-\psi^{-2}|d\psi|_{\bar h}^2$ cancels the gradient-square terms and gives $R(h)=\psi^{-5}(\bar R\psi-8\Delta_{\bar h}\psi)$.

Substituting steps 1.3 and 1.4 into the left side of the SI Hamiltonian constraint [F2], and step 1.2 into its right side, gives $\psi^{-5}(-8\Delta_{\bar h}\psi+\bar R\psi)-\psi^{-12}|\bar A|_{\bar h}^2+\frac{2}{3}\tau^2=2\Lambda+2\psi^{-8}(|\bar E|_{\bar h}^2+|\bar B|_{\bar h}^2)$. Multiplication by the positive $\psi^5$ is reversible and yields exactly the transformed scalar equation in the Statement; step 1.1 gives the two equivalent Maxwell constraints.

By step 1.2, the right side of the SI momentum constraint in [F2] is $-2\psi^{-6}(\bar E\times_{\bar h}\bar B)_i$, which proves the displayed retained momentum equation. If $K=0$, its left side vanishes; if also $\bar E\times_{\bar h}\bar B=0$, its right side vanishes. No step has inferred this vector equation from the scalar constraint.

derivations.claim: Put $C:=m^2-q^2$ and $w:=\psi^2$. Since $2r+m>0$, the condition $w>0$ is equivalent to $2r+m>|q|$, giving exactly $\mathcal D_{m,q}$. Thus $\psi$ is smooth and positive there. In Euclidean spherical coordinates, $\bar D_i\bar E^i=r^{-2}\partial_r(r^2 q r^{-2})=0$, while $\bar D_i\bar B^i=0$.

On this domain $w:=\psi^2=1+m/r+C/(4r^2)$, $w'=-m/r^2-C/(2r^3)$, and $w''=2m/r^3+3C/(2r^4)$. Since $\Delta_{\mathbb R^3}\psi=\psi''+2\psi'/r$, $\psi'/\psi=w'/(2w)$ and $\psi''/\psi=w''/(2w)-(w')^2/(4w^2)$ give $\Delta_{\mathbb R^3}\psi/\psi=(w''/2+w'/r)/w-(w')^2/(4w^2)=(Cw/r^4-(w')^2)/(4w^2)=-q^2/(4r^4w^2)$; here $w''/2+w'/r=C/(4r^4)$ and direct expansion gives $Cw/r^4-(w')^2=-q^2/r^4$. Thus $\Delta_{\mathbb R^3}\psi=-q^2/(4r^4\psi^3)$. With $\bar R=0$, $\bar A=\tau=\Lambda=\bar B=0$, the transformed scalar equation is $-8\Delta\psi-2q^2r^{-4}\psi^{-3}=0$.

The seed Gauss constraint holds by step 1.1, and step 1.2 verifies the Hamiltonian equation. The momentum right side vanishes because $\bar B=0$, and its left side vanishes because $K=\tau=0$. The omitted point $r=0$ is not in the manifold, so the smooth divergence calculation on $\mathcal D_{m,q}\times S^2$ makes no distributional assertion at the puncture.

Suppose $m>|q|$, so $C>0$ and $r_0=\sqrt C/2$. Then $R_{\rm areal}=r+m+C/(4r)$, $R'_{\rm areal}=1-C/(4r^2)$, and $R''_{\rm areal}=C/(2r^3)>0$. Hence $R_{\rm areal}$ has its unique minimum on $(0,\infty)$ at $r_0$, with value $m+\sqrt C$. The area formula follows directly from the induced metric on $S_r$, namely $r^2\psi^4\gamma_{S^2}$.

The outward unit normal to $S_r$ is $\nu=\psi^{-2}\partial_r$. Its mean curvature, defined as the trace of the second fundamental form, is $H=\operatorname{div}_h\nu=(\sqrt{\det h})^{-1}\partial_r(\sqrt{\det h}\,\psi^{-2})=2R'_{\rm areal}/(\psi^2R_{\rm areal})$. Thus $H(r_0)=0$, and $H$ is nonzero for every other centered coordinate sphere.

Write $r_0^2=C/4$ and $R=R_{\rm areal}(r)$. On $r>r_0$, $R>m+2r_0$, so $f(R)>0$. Direct algebra gives $R^2f(R)=(R-m)^2-C=(r-r_0^2/r)^2$ and $dR/dr=1-r_0^2/r^2=(r-r_0^2/r)/r$. Therefore $f(R)^{-1}(dR/dr)^2=R^2/r^2=\psi^4$, which proves that $h=\psi^4dr^2+R^2\gamma_{S^2}$ equals the radial and angular spatial metric in [F3] on this branch.

As $r\to\infty$, $\psi^4=1+2m/r+O(r^{-2})$; differentiating this explicit rational expression for $\psi^4$ gives first- and second-coordinate-derivative falloffs $O(r^{-2})$ and $O(r^{-3})$. For the inner end put $\tilde r=r_0^2/r$. Then $\psi(r)^2r^2/r_0^2=1+m/\tilde r+r_0^2/\tilde r^2=\psi(\tilde r)^2$ and $dr^2+r^2\gamma_{S^2}=(r^4/r_0^4)(d\tilde r^2+\tilde r^2\gamma_{S^2})$. Hence the inner metric is exactly the same isotropic form in $\tilde r$, and it has the same falloff and derivative estimates. This proves the two stated end descriptions without extending the static areal chart through $f=0$.

For $m>|q|$, $\mathcal D_{m,q}=(0,\infty)$. The centered coordinate sphere $S_r=\{r\}\times S^2$ has area $4\pi R_{\rm areal}(r)^2$, where

$$R_{\rm areal}(r):=r\psi(r)^2=r+m+\frac{m^2-q^2}{4r}.$$

It has zero mean curvature exactly at $r_0=\frac12\sqrt{m^2-q^2}$, and $R_{\rm areal}(r_0)=m+\sqrt{m^2-q^2}$

derivations.claim: Substituting $q^2=m^2$ into the conformal factor gives $\psi^2=(1+m/(2r))^2-m^2/(4r^2)=1+m/r$, which is positive for every $r>0$. Therefore $\rho=r\psi^2=r+m$ and $\rho'(r)=1$.

The radial line element of $h=\psi^4(dr^2+r^2\gamma_{S^2})$ is $\psi^2dr=(1+m/r)dr$. Since $s'(r)=1+m/r=\psi^2>0$, $s$ is a proper radial coordinate; moreover $s\to-\infty$ as $r\downarrow0$ and $s\to+\infty$ as $r\to\infty$, so its range is $\mathbb R$.

Replacing $\psi^4dr^2$ by $ds^2$ and using $\rho=r+m$ gives $h=ds^2+\rho(s)^2\gamma_{S^2}$. As $s\to-\infty$, $r(s)\to0$, so $\rho(s)^2\to m^2$ and the spherical coefficient converges to that of the product cylinder of radius $m$.

The unit normal to $S_r$ is $\nu=\psi^{-2}\partial_r$. Its mean curvature is $H=\operatorname{div}_h\nu=2\rho'/(\psi^2\rho)=2r/(r+m)^2>0$ for every $r>0$. Thus no centered coordinate sphere is minimal, while the infinite negative range of $s$ proves that the puncture is an infinite-distance cylindrical end.

citations.quote: The exact vector divergence identities are $D_iE^i=\psi^{-6}\bar D_i\bar E^i$ and $D_iB^i=\psi^{-6}\bar D_i\bar B^i$. The separate momentum constraint remains

derivations.claim: The seed vector $\bar E=\partial_x$ has Euclidean divergence $\bar D_i\bar E^i=\partial_x(1)=0$, so it satisfies the source-free seed Gauss condition. The function $\psi=e^x$ is smooth and positive on all of $\mathbb R^3$.

If instead one assigns the unscaled vector $E=\bar E$, then $\sqrt{\det h}=\psi^6=e^{6x}$ and the coordinate divergence formula gives $D_iE^i=(\sqrt{\det h})^{-1}\partial_i(\sqrt{\det h}\,E^i)=e^{-6x}\partial_x(e^{6x})=6$. Thus the claimed universal preservation fails: this smooth field violates $D_iE^i=0$ everywhere.

The correct conformal field is $E=\psi^{-6}\bar E=e^{-6x}\partial_x$, for which step 1.1's seed identity gives $D_iE^i=e^{-6x}\bar D_i\bar E^i=0$. Hence the counterexample isolates the missing vector weight and uses no singular source at a removed point.
